## 🌎 Geopolitics

### Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan forge mutual defense pact amid Iranian pressure

The leaders of Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan signed a joint defense agreement Friday in Mecca, binding the three nations through Article 5-style collective defense: any armed attack on one triggers automatic defense by all. Turkey brings NATO's second-largest military; Saudi Arabia controls roughly 13% of global oil exports; Pakistan holds the Islamic world's sole nuclear arsenal. The pact follows nearly a year of back-channel negotiations and comes as Saudi Arabia faces escalating drone and missile strikes from Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen and proxy militias in Iraq.

**Why it matters.** This reshapes the power balance in South Asia and the Middle East in ways that directly affect India's strategic calculations. Pakistan—India's nuclear-armed neighbor with whom Delhi has fought four wars—just gained formal defensive backing from NATO's regional anchor and the Middle East's energy heavyweight. For a consulting practitioner tracking emerging-market geopolitics, this signals hardening blocs: India can no longer assume it operates in a unipolar security environment. The pact also locks Saudi Arabia into a tighter embrace with Ankara, potentially complicating India's independent oil diplomacy in the Gulf. Quant strategies betting on South Asian political stability face higher tail risk.

**Action.** Monitor India's official response and whether New Delhi moves to deepen ties with Saudi Arabia as a counterweight. Track Pakistan's military posture for elevated readiness signaling. Watch whether the alliance expands to Egypt or other states as Turkey's foreign minister suggested; a broader MENA coalition would fragment India's diplomatic options in the region. Cross-reference with Indian refinery purchasing and LNG flows from Saudi suppliers—pricing could shift if regional tensions escalate.

*Sources: [atlanticcouncil.org](https://www.atlanticcouncil.org/dispatches/why-saudi-arabia-pakistan-and-turkey-just-signed-a-defense-pact/) · [breakingdefense.com](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/08/saudi-arabia-turkey-pakistan-ink-joint-defense-agreement/) · [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/7/saudi-%e2%81%a0arabia-pakistan-and-turkiye-sign-defence-deal-amid-regional-turmoil)*

### Trump signals imminent Iran deal on Strait of Hormuz as talks stall over sanctions withdrawal

President Trump stated Sunday that a Strait of Hormuz reopening agreement with Iran could come "soon," while simultaneously admitting Washington is only "semi-negotiating" with Tehran. Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary issued a competing set of demands: full lift of the US naval blockade, complete sanctions removal, total US military withdrawal from the region, war reparations, and return of frozen assets. The standoff caps a month of deteriorating talks; as of August 10, Iran has replaced senior military leadership and Houthi strikes on Saudi vessels continue unabated. The US has now imposed eight rounds of sanctions on Iran in 2026 alone, including Treasury measures targeting shadow-banking networks and crypto-facilitated illicit finance.

**Why it matters.** The Strait of Hormuz moves 15-20% of global seaborne oil; any reopening or collapse of talks reshapes energy prices within weeks and directly impacts India's import costs and refinery exposure. India sources roughly 3 million barrels per day from the Gulf region and buys Iranian crude through workarounds; deal terms matter enormously to Delhi's energy security calculus and rupee-denominated energy costs. For a quant analyst, this is a high-vol political event that moves Brent and WTI futures in both directions—Trump's "semi-negotiating" language suggests unpredictable dealmaking rather than traditional diplomacy, raising volatility premia. Secondary sanctions risk also matters: Indian refineries and traders operating Iranian crude face compliance exposure if US terms harden.

**Action.** Set alerts on Brent crude (WTI) for breakout moves on any Trump announcement; track official Indian government statements on sanctions compliance. Read the latest from FDD's Iran Iran Sanctions Team and Council on Foreign Relations' Iran tracker for negotiation details. Monitor whether the US signals willingness to trade sanctions relief for Hormuz access—if so, expect immediate crude sell-off and rupee stability. Cross-check Indian refinery purchasing patterns for any hedging moves ahead of deal announcement.

*Sources: [cnn.com](https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/10/world/live-news/iran-war-trump) · [foxnews.com](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/iran-war-us-trump-strait-of-hormuz-08-07-2026) · [forbes.com](https://www.forbes.com/sites/maryroeloffs/2026/08/08/iran-says-us-must-meet-demands-before-strait-of-hormuz-reopens/)*

## 🧠 Artificial Intelligence

### Meta Releases Muse Glimmer, a 30B Open-Weight Agent Model for Consumer GPU Inference

Meta released Muse Glimmer on August 10, 2026, a 30-billion-parameter open-source model optimized for agentic workflows that runs entirely on a single consumer GPU—RTX 5090, Mac M5 Max, or equivalent. The model uses a novel DFlash inference technique achieving 3.1x speedup on RTX 5090 and 1.8x on Apple Silicon, with the 4-bit quantized version fitting in 24–32GB memory. Muse Glimmer scores 75.5 on MCP-Atlas (multi-step tool orchestration), 74.6 on DeepSearch QA, 51.2 on SWE-Bench Pro, and 94.7 on AIME 2026, outperforming Gemma4-31B and Qwen3.6-27B across agentic and reasoning tasks.

**Why it matters.** Local agent inference breaks the cloud-dependent model for production AI agents. Until now, running complex multi-step agents required cloud infrastructure—fixed cost, latency risk, vendor lock-in. Muse Glimmer on a $2k GPU means you can run full agent loops (tool calls, function composition, code execution) on premise or on-device. For latency-sensitive agents (real-time trading, autonomous robotics, edge deployment), this is a 10x improvement over API-call round trips. For enterprises, this eliminates vendor dependency in agentic workflows. The open Apache 2.0 release means fine-tuning and deployment are unencumbered—a direct challenge to OpenAI's and Anthropic's proprietary agent models.

**Action.** If you're building agent infrastructure, benchmark Muse Glimmer against your current cloud-based agent stack—measure latency, cost-per-task, and throughput. If you're already working with inference optimization (quantization, speculative decoding), the DFlash technique is worth reading; the speedup suggests architectural gains beyond just throughput. For production agents, test whether 30B parameter density is sufficient for your tool-calling and reasoning demands; SWE-Bench Pro at 51.2 is solid but not frontier-class code generation.

*Sources: [research.meta.ai](https://research.meta.ai/blog/introducing-muse-glimmer-open-agentic-model) · [techtimes.com](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/323787/20260810/meta-launches-muse-glimmer-first-consumer-gpu-agent-model-built-autonomous-tasks.htm) · [neowin.net](https://www.neowin.net/news/meta-releases-muse-glimmer-a-30b-open-agentic-ai-model-that-runs-locally-on-pcs/)*

### Google Rolls Out Voice Agents Calling Stores, Checking Inventory, and Completing Retail Transactions

Google launched autonomous voice agents on August 10, 2026 that call retail stores on behalf of consumers to check inventory, compare prices, and complete purchases with merchant consent. The feature integrates into Google Search via a "Let Google Call" prompt: users search for a product, and the agent calls local retailers, gathers availability and pricing data, and can execute a transaction. This marks the first production deployment of autonomous agents directly executing commerce transactions at scale—moving agents from benchmarks and internal demos into live economic workflows.

**Why it matters.** Agents are now generating revenue and closing transactions in real time. For months, the AI field has debated whether current-generation agents are reliable enough for production—this answers the question by putting skin in the game: Google is now liable for agent failures (incorrect inventory lookups, botched transactions, customer experience). For infrastructure builders, this signals demand for robust multi-turn agent orchestration, error recovery, and human-in-the-loop handoff. For enterprises, it forces a reckoning on agent readiness: if Google is confident enough to let agents handle $50–$200 retail transactions, your enterprise agent pilots may need to accelerate. For the retail sector, this creates immediate pressure to implement agent-compatible APIs (inventory APIs, transaction APIs) to avoid losing customer interactions to aggregators.

**Action.** If you're in retail or supply chain, audit whether your inventory and purchasing systems expose clean APIs that agents can call—Google's agents will target the most accessible retailers. If you're building agentic systems internally, study the error modes Google must be handling (inventory race conditions, authorization failures, customer disputes) because those are now blocking other agents too. If you're on the infrastructure side, agent orchestration frameworks now need explicit transaction rollback and dispute logging—the stakes shifted from "wrong answer" to "financial liability."

## 🇮🇳 India

### Aum Ventures Closes ₹225 Crore for India's New Deeptech Fund as Foreign Capital Floods In

Aum Ventures announced on August 10 the first close of India Innovation Fund II at ₹225 crore ($23.6 million), with a total target of ₹750 crore. The fund will invest in early-stage startups across AI, space tech, semiconductors, aerospace, defence, and robotics. Over 65% of capital in the first close came from international limited partners—family offices, entrepreneurs, and strategic investors from the US, Middle East, and other markets—signalling growing confidence in India as a deeptech destination.

**Why it matters.** If you're building AI infrastructure, autonomous systems, or space tech in India, this fund represents a meaningful shift: deep-pocketed foreign capital now sees India's research talent and regulatory environment as credible for frontier technologies. Aum plans to deploy initial cheques of $750,000 to $2 million into 25-30 companies, with follow-on capital reserved for Series A/B. This removes a historical funding bottleneck for hardware founders and research-heavy teams who struggled to raise under $5 million from traditional Indian VCs.

**Action.** Monitor Aum's portfolio announcements through August-September as they deploy the remaining ₹525 crore. If your deeptech startup is pre-Series A (or raising $1-2M), review Aum's thesis on Github, arXiv citations, or founder backgrounds of their prior portfolio (Skyroot, Cosmoserve, Latent AI, Sully.ai). Track whether ₹750 crore closes fully—it'll signal whether foreign LPs maintain conviction on India's deeptech timeline amid global tech cycles.

### Shiprocket IPO Opens Tomorrow at ₹92–97, Targeting ₹7,000 Crore as Logistics Solidifies

Shiprocket, India's largest end-to-end logistics startup, opens its ₹1,617.48 crore IPO on August 12 at a price band of ₹92 to ₹97 per share, with listing tentatively set for August 19. The issue comprises ₹885.5 crore in fresh shares and ₹731.98 crore in offer-for-sale from existing shareholders. For FY26, Shiprocket reported ₹2,077.42 crore in revenue (24% year-on-year growth) and a net loss of ₹79.25 crore.

**Why it matters.** Logistics is the plumbing of AI: every consumer-facing startup—marketplace, SaaS, lending, on-demand—depends on last-mile execution. Shiprocket's IPO at a deliberate 30% discount to its last private valuation signals investor caution on SaaS-logistics unit economics, but the fact that it's proceeding (and 24 companies are targeting ₹35,000 crore in August IPOs collectively) means the ecosystem believes logistics margins stabilize once you hit scale. If you're building a fintech, commerce, or delivery product, Shiprocket's FY26 performance—and how it trades post-listing—will set expectations for logistics cost as % of GMV, regulatory risk, and working capital requirements for the next 18 months.

**Action.** Pull Shiprocket's DRHP filing from SEBI's website to review revenue per shipment, unit economics by geography, and customer concentration. Track the opening-day subscription ratio (target is 1.5–2x normally)—low subscription would signal investor doubt about SaaS-logistics profitability, which ripples through expense budgets for logistics-dependent startups. Monitor the August 19 listing closely: if it closes below ₹92, it reflects broader wariness of platform SaaS; if it closes 20% above, it may spark a second wave of logistics IPO filings.

*Sources: [[TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/322767/20260803/shiprocket-eyes-august-ipo-at-measured-valuation-after-slashing-losses-88.htm)]([TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/322767/20260803/shiprocket-eyes-august-ipo-at-measured-valuation-after-slashing-losses-88.htm)) · [[Whalesbook](https://www.whalesbook.com/news/English/transportation/Shiprocket-IPO-Opens-Aug-12-Price-Band-Set-at-indian-rupee92-97/6a7402453b2431b2558607e9)]([Whalesbook](https://www.whalesbook.com/news/English/transportation/Shiprocket-IPO-Opens-Aug-12-Price-Band-Set-at-indian-rupee92-97/6a7402453b2431b2558607e9)) · [[Outlook Business](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/markets/shiprocket-ipo-who-is-cashing-in-where-885-cr-will-go-and-what-could-go-wrong)]([Outlook Business](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/markets/shiprocket-ipo-who-is-cashing-in-where-885-cr-will-go-and-what-could-go-wrong))*

## 📈 Markets

### Iran-Oman Diplomacy Offers Relief, But Oil Stays Elevated as Inflation Risks Keep US Equities Checked

The Strait of Hormuz eased back from crisis mode on August 10 as Iran and Oman pursued diplomatic talks, allowing a modest pullback in crude—Brent settled at $87.69/barrel, up 4.95% from the prior session but below recent highs. US indices surrendered early gains: S&P 500 closed at 7,753.11 (−0.06%), Nasdaq −0.3%, Dow −0.1%. Indian equities ended nearly flat with Nifty 50 at 24,583.80 (+0.05%) and Sensex at 78,542.44 (+0.06%), while Bank Nifty finished at 57,686. The US 10-year Treasury held steady at 4.65% as markets weighed whether energy supply normalization could ease wage-price pressures. INR/USD moved to 95.24, up 0.11%, as global capital recalibrated risk.

**Why it matters.** For Indian markets, the Strait deconflation signals potential relief from imported energy costs, a structural drag on rupee stability and real rates. Gold's surge to $4,378.76/oz (+0.81%) underscores persistent safe-haven demand despite diplomatic thaw—when geopolitical risk remains priced in and global liquidity is tightening, tech and rate-sensitive names face headwinds. For AI infrastructure plays, US inflation persistence (the actual driver of the Nasdaq sell) matters more than Middle East theater: sustained yields above 4.5% and PCE concerns keep capital allocation tilted toward commodity and energy exposure over duration assets.

**Action.** Watch the August 14 US CPI print for wage-inflation dynamics and Fed pivot signals. Oil's critical level: hold $85 and risk remains geopolitical; break $80 and you have real supply relief. Track INR through 95.50 on rupee stability; RBI's recent growth revision to 6.7% suggests confidence, but sticky 10Y yields could force liquidity tightening if CPI disappoints. RBI MPC meets end-month; no immediate move expected but Fed dots on September cuts will dominate the call.

### RBI's Growth Confidence Meets Sticky Yield Reality as Safe-Haven Bid Lifts Gold, Pressures Carry Trades

The RBI raised its full-year growth forecast to 6.7% from 6.6% in early August, signaling confidence in monsoon recovery and domestic demand resilience. Yet bond markets are pricing rate persistence: the US 10-year held at 4.65% despite disinflation whispers, keeping real yields punitive for EM duration. Gold rose to $4,378.76/oz, the highest in weeks, as investors hedged duration and geopolitical tail risk. The rupee weakened to 95.24 against the dollar, a near-term pressure that undercuts the bull case for Indian rate cuts—if INR slips into the 96 handle and oil stays above $85, RBI's next move (likely a cut) becomes constrained by currency stability.

**Why it matters.** For prop and macro research, this is the critical arbitrage: RBI's growth view (bullish for re-acceleration) conflicts with its transmission channel (tightening financial conditions). High yields abroad and geopolitical risk premiums in commodities mean EM fixed-income carry trades unwind as dollar rates stay bid. The 6.7% growth print may be priced in, but forward guidance on rate cuts—if hawkish on the rupee—could surprise consensus. This is the kind of second-order macro shift that reshuffles risk allocation: rotation out of rate-cut plays into commodity/energy hedges or commodity-linked equities.

**Action.** Track the RBI's next MPC statement for commentary on rupee management vs. growth support. If CPI next week (US) prints hot, expect US yields to spike further, pressuring INR below 95.50. Gold above $4,400 signals sustained geopolitical premium; break $4,250 and you have real safe-haven unwinding. Watch implied vol in USD/INR: if skew widens to the downside, institutional hedging is intensifying ahead of monsoon risk or Fed signal season.

## 🇮🇳 Indian Stocks

### TITAN (NSE): +3.6% on stellar Q1 jewellery expansion

Titan Company surged to a record ₹5,033.90 on August 10, 2026, closing near ₹4,998 as investors digested a robust June quarter. Consolidated net profit jumped 65% year-on-year to ₹1,699 crore, while revenue expanded 29.3% to ₹21,356 crore. Trading volume tracked earnings release activity. The domestic jewellery division posted a 38% revenue surge despite the customs duty hike, signalling strong underlying demand.

**Why it matters.** Titan's jewellery beat—especially the 31% jump in transaction values—rewrites sentiment on discretionary spending. This signals consumer resilience in urban India after monsoon concerns weighed on broader sentiment. The sector read-across matters: if premium consumption holds despite inflation headwinds, the FMCG and luxury goods complex may outperform dividend-heavy sectors in Q2 diagnostics. For a Hyderabad-based tech engineer tracking domestic allocations, this suggests retail holding power even as geopolitical tension clouds crude prices.

**Action.** Check Titan's BSE announcement filing (ref: consolidated FY27 Q1 results, filed August 8) for segment-level jewellery and watches EBITDA margins to confirm whether the 38% revenue beat came with margin compression or expansion. Brokerages targeted ₹5,500–₹6,000 on the results, setting resistance. Monitor the next block deal trackers for insider/promoter activity.

### BAJFINANCE (NSE): +6.5% on Q1 profit beat; loan growth accelerates

Bajaj Finance surged to ₹1,122 on NSE on July 31–August 1, gaining 6.5% on the back of Q1 FY27 profit that beat consensus. Net profit grew 29% year-on-year to ₹5,436 crore, while net interest income—the engine of lending profitability—jumped 24% to ₹11,495 crore. Non-interest income rose 18% year-on-year, signalling diversification into lending-adjacent businesses. Volume tracked earnings release; the stock hit a 52-week high.

**Why it matters.** Bajaj Finance's 29% earnings growth in a moderating rate environment signals the lender is gaining market share in unsecured lending (personal loans, credit cards, buy-now-pay-later). The 24% NII beat suggests pricing power and disciplined credit risk management. For sector watchers, this validates the NBFC/HFC trade: growth is shifting from bank deposits to shadow lenders as rate cycles tighten. The stock's prominence in Nifty 50 weightings means this beat lifts the broader index's Q1 earnings resilience narrative, with read-across to ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank positioning.

**Action.** Pull Bajaj Finance's earnings call transcript (posted August 4, 2026; search "Bajaj Finance Q1 FY27 earnings call") to track loan-to-deposit ratios, slippage rates (90+ DPD), and the cost of funds trend—all critical to sustainability of the 29% beat. Brokerage price targets moved to ₹1,150 (from ₹1,035), implying 9% upside at the time; watch for resistance at ₹1,200 and ₹1,250 on any index strength.

## 🩹 Health & Science

### Oral GLP-1 Pill Achieves 12% Weight Loss in Phase 2b Trial, Expanding Treatment Beyond Injectables

Structure Therapeutics' aleniglipron, a once-daily oral GLP-1 receptor agonist, produced mean weight reductions of 12.1% over 36 weeks in a randomized, double-blind, phase 2b trial of 230 adults with obesity or overweight—compared to 0.5% with placebo. Extended data showed 16.2% weight loss at 56 weeks with the 120 mg dose. As a small-molecule pill versus injectable competitors like Wegovy and Ozempic, the drug addresses adherence barriers inherent to subcutaneous administration.

**Why it matters.** This represents a genuine inflection in obesity pharmacotherapy. Injectables dominate the current GLP-1 market but face cold-chain logistics, patient discomfort, and adherence friction. Oral formulation at comparable efficacy unlocks a broader addressable market—particularly in underserved regions and populations averse to injections. For healthcare AI builders, this signals demand for digital adherence tools, dose-optimization algorithms, and cardiovascular risk stratification in weight-loss cohorts. For clinicians, it validates once-daily oral GLP-1s as a viable next-generation therapy, shifting what's possible in primary-care obesity management.

**Action.** Read the trial results in Nature Medicine (aleniglipron Phase 2b study). Structure Therapeutics is initiating Phase 3 in H2 2026; track regulatory milestones for oral GLP-1 comparator data. For organizations building metabolic health platforms, model cost-of-goods and adherence curves for oral versus injectable GLP-1s to forecast market capture. Clinicians should begin discussing oral GLP-1 as a realistic alternative for appropriate patients during the 18-24 month Phase 3 window.

*Sources: [[Nature Medicine - Aleniglipron Phase 2b Trial](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04476-6)]([Nature Medicine - Aleniglipron Phase 2b Trial](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04476-6)) · [[ScienceDaily - Oral GLP-1 Delivers 12% Weight Loss](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/08/260810015717.htm)]([ScienceDaily - Oral GLP-1 Delivers 12% Weight Loss](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/08/260810015717.htm)) · [[BioPharma Dive - Structure GLP-1 Pill Results](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/structure-glp1-aleniglipron-study-results-obesity/814786/)]([BioPharma Dive - Structure GLP-1 Pill Results](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/structure-glp1-aleniglipron-study-results-obesity/814786/))*

### Elevated Lipoprotein(a) Identified as Major Cardiovascular Risk Factor in 20,000-Person Analysis; Screening Urged Despite Controlled LDL

A meta-analysis of three NIH randomized controlled trials (ACCORD, PEACE, SPRINT) involving 20,070 adults age 40 and older found that elevated lipoprotein(a)—an inherited cholesterol particle—substantially increased risk of cardiovascular death and stroke, even among patients with well-controlled LDL. Individuals with Lp(a) levels of 175 nmol/L or higher showed significantly elevated residual cardiovascular risk. The finding surprised researchers because roughly 20% of the population carries elevated Lp(a), yet most remain unaware due to lack of symptoms.

**Why it matters.** This shifts Lp(a) from academic curiosity to actionable screening metric. Current cardiovascular risk models (Framingham, ACC/AHA) largely ignore Lp(a), leaving a blind spot in millions at genetic risk. The discovery of "statin-resistant" cardiovascular events in those with controlled LDL but elevated Lp(a) opens a new risk stratification dimension. For AI health platforms, this signals opportunity: Lp(a) screening + family history algorithms can identify high-risk cohorts earlier and cheaper than waiting for clinical events. For pharmaceutical companies, it justifies Lp(a)-lowering drugs (peripical, inclisiran) and companion diagnostics.

**Action.** Clinicians should add Lp(a) to baseline lipid panels for patients 40+ with family history of early MI/stroke, or those whose LDL is well-controlled yet cardiovascular events occur. Data was presented at SCAI 2026 in Montreal—review conference proceedings for effect sizes and adjusted hazard ratios. Organizations building preventive-health infrastructure should flag 175+ nmol/L thresholds for automated referral to lipidology. Startups should model reimbursement pathways for Lp(a) testing plus risk counseling in primary care.

**Why it matters.** In an era fragmented by algorithm-driven streaming, Grande's dominant first-week numbers signal that superstardom still drives coordinated listener behavior across platforms. This reflects not just fanbase loyalty but the consolidated power of major-label marketing and playlist placement in 2026's streamed-music economy. For distribution strategists, Grande's sustained dominance across both US and UK markets suggests legacy artists remain immune to the mid-tier erosion plaguing the middle class of musicians.

**Action.** Track whether "petal" sustains playlist velocity into September—if streaming drop-off mirrors traditional album decline or if her platform advantage keeps week-two momentum stronger than typical. ### "Coyote vs. ACME" Finally Releases After Warner Bros. Killed It for a Tax Write-Off

Three years after Warner Bros. shelved "Coyote vs. ACME" with a $30 million tax write-off in 2023, the live-action animation hybrid comedy is seeing theatrical distribution on August 21 (UK/Ireland) and August 28 (US) through Ketchup Entertainment. The studio acquired the Dave Green–directed film for $50 million in March 2025—a wager that the James Gunn-penned property could find an audience as a specialized release rather than a tentpole.

**Why it matters.** This is a tell about theatrical economics in 2026. Major studios no longer own theatrical failure; they abandon projects and absorb the loss. Ketchup Entertainment's $50 million acquisition is a bet that niche distributors can monetize what studios deem disposable—and that nostalgia IP (Looney Tunes) still moves tickets. The casting of Will Forte, Lana Condor, John Cena, and Luis Guzman suggests Ketchup positioned this as prestige comedy rather than kids' fare, a repositioning that reflects how studio franchises now seek adult-skewing distribution channels.

**Action.** Watch the per-theater average on opening weekend—success here defines whether live-action/animation hybrids have a viable theatrical lane post-streaming. If "Coyote" clears $15M domestically, expect acceleration in studios selling "dead" projects to specialty distributors rather than writing them off. If it underperforms, the model collapses and the shelving strategy returns.
